Subject: Contoso: SKU mapping + technical items for Azure offer submission

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for taking this on. We're trying to get our initial offer submitted to the Azure Marketplace this week. A few open items on the tech/portal side that we need help clarifying: 

- SKU mapping: We have three commercial SKUs (Starter, Professional, Enterprise). Which SKU type should be mapped to Plan vs. Metered SKUs in the publisher portal to enable co-sell tagging?
- State transitions: After we update the offer in the portal, what is the typical lifecycle (how long until the offer is visible in the catalog vs. published to customers)?
- Technical validation: we attached the manifest and network architecture. Are there specific configuration flags in the offer JSON we should change to avoid rejections during the technical gate?

Attachments: contoso-offer-manifest.json (v1), network-architecture.pdf

If helpful we can do a 30-minute screen share today. We're on PT.

Best,
Anika Shah

anika.shah@contoso-retail.com

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Contoso: SKU mapping + technical items for Azure offer submission

Hi Anika — thanks for the details and the attachments. Looping in Marissa (marketplace enablement) and Karthik (engineering) to ensure we cover both the commercial mapping and the technical gate. Quick answers up front: 

- SKU mapping: For co-sell readiness we usually map your three commercial SKUs to three Plans (Starter/Pro/Ent) in the Offer artifact. Metered SKUs are better when you bill by usage; since Contoso plans are seat-based, Plans are the right fit. We can add metering later if you add usage-based tiers.

- Visibility/lifecycle: After submission the portal runs a validation pass (24–48 hrs typically). If it passes technical checks and legal/commercial review, the offer moves to the Pending/Publish state. From Publish -> Marketplace listing can take an additional 24–48 hrs once certified. So plan for ~3–5 business days if nothing is flagged.

- Technical validation: Karthik — any obvious manifest flags to call out?

Next steps I propose:
1) Karthik to scan the manifest for required fields and a quick flag pass.
2) Marissa to confirm the co-sell tag workflow and which Plan IDs to attach.
3) Anika to upload the corrected manifest to the portal and reply here when done.

If you want the deeper checklist I can send the MSFT validation checklist and a short runbook for submission.

Evelyn Hart
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Contoso: SKU mapping + technical items for Azure offer submission

Hi Anika — adding a few practical steps from the marketplace side: 

- Plan IDs: Create three Plan entries in your offer (planId values must be stable strings). We recommend planId values like contoso-starter, contoso-pro, contoso-enterprise. Those map cleanly to co-sell records.
- Co-sell tagging: When you submit the offer, under Marketplace Properties enable "Co-sell (Marketplace)" and provide your resale/lift contact. Microsoft will review; to expedite, include partner center IDs and your seller profile page link.
- Price lists: For initial submission pick list prices in USD; the portal accepts multi-currency mappings later.
- Network/VM config: Karthik, per the attached network diagram, please confirm there are no inbound-only endpoints that would fail validation.

I'll also upload the msft-checklist.xlsx to the thread — it lists the common manifest schema failures I see.

Marissa Cole
Marketplace Programs, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

1) Portal flags and artifact updates: If the portal returns technical validation errors, Contoso will need to re-upload the corrected manifest from your publisher account. However, Redwood can prepare the corrected artifact (we already scanned v1.1) and share it as a zip; if you grant us delegated publishing rights in the publisher portal we can upload on your behalf. I'll include a short step list below for granting delegated access.

2) Co-sell timing: Recommend enabling co-sell at initial submission to avoid a second round of reviews. As Marissa noted, include Partner Center IDs and any reseller contacts to speed the MSFT review.

We can prioritize the review on our side — Marissa and Karthik will do a targeted pass within 24 hours. Microsoft support, can you confirm expected validation ETA if we mark co-sell enabled?

Next steps (agreed):
- Contoso grants delegated publisher access to evelyn.hart@redwood.ai (Portal > Account Settings > Delegates).
- Contoso uploads final manifest with planIds as discussed and sets Co-sell toggle ON.
- Redwood will perform a final local validation and be on standby for portal errors.
- Microsoft to confirm publish ETA for co-sell-enabled offers.

I also shared a DocuSign link for the publisher delegation MOU — please sign if you want Redwood to be able to publish on your behalf: https://www.docusign.com/complete/example-docu-sign-link

Thanks — we'll aim to complete the internal pass today so you can submit tomorrow and keep the March deadline.
